_readme: Curated library of publicly reported subsea infrastructure incidents.
Purpose is calibration, not accusation. A detection means nothing until a reader can
compare it against cases whose outcomes are known - including the cases that were
investigated and closed as accidents, and the cases where a vessel was boarded and
released. Those are deliberately over-represented here. A tool that only shows you
confirmed sabotage teaches you to see sabotage everywhere.
Coordinates are APPROXIMATE unless marked otherwise. They are derived from press
reporting, not from official incident positions, and are good to roughly 10-30 km.
They are adequate for placing a marker on a map and inadequate for anything else.
'status' uses: CHARGED, CONVICTED, DETAINED, INVESTIGATING, RELEASED_NO_EVIDENCE,
Adding a case: append an object, run `python -m grapnel.publish`, open a PR. Every
claim needs at least one source URL. Claims sourced only to social media are rejected.

incidents.title: Balticconnector pipeline and EE-S1 telecom cable, Gulf of Finland
incidents.mechanism: Anchor drag; anchor recovered from the seabed
incidents.outcome: China acknowledged after several months that the vessel was responsible and characterised the damage as accidental.
incidents.why_it_matters: First case in the Baltic series to be physically confirmed by recovering the ground tackle. Establishes the anchor-drag mechanism that every later case is compared against.

sources.label: NBC News - suspicion falls on Russian and Chinese vessels
Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists - Seabed zero

incidents.title: Taiwan-Matsu Islands cables severed
incidents.vessel: Chinese fishing vessel and freighter (not individually identified in public reporting)
incidents.outcome: Roughly 14,000 residents lost internet for weeks. Taiwanese authorities named Chinese vessels but stopped short of calling it deliberate.
incidents.why_it_matters: Shows the second-order cost: small island communities have no redundancy, so a cable cut is a total outage rather than a latency increase.

incidents.title: C-Lion1 and BCS East-West Interlink cut near Oland and Gotland
incidents.mechanism: Anchor dragged approximately 300 km across both cable routes
incidents.outcome: Vessel shadowed and later allowed to depart. No prosecution reported.
incidents.why_it_matters: The canonical drag signature: a sustained, straight, sub-transit-speed track across two separate routes. This is the behaviour the anchor_drag detector is tuned against.

incidents.title: Yantar operating over cables and pipelines in the Irish Sea
assets: Multiple telecom and power cables east of Dublin and south-west of the Isle of Man
incidents.mechanism: Survey and loitering. No damage attributed.
incidents.outcome: Escorted out of the Irish EEZ by the Irish military; separately shadowed by the Royal Navy on other transits.
incidents.why_it_matters: The case that shows the limit of this tool. Yantar is operated by Russia's Main Directorate of Deep Sea Research and is assessed to be a mothership for deep-diving submersibles. Whatever those submersibles do is invisible to AIS. The surface track is the only observable, and a survey track is not evidence of a tap.

sources.label: Data Center Dynamics - Irish military escorts Yantar

incidents.title: Estlink 2 power cable and four telecom cables, Gulf of Finland
incidents.outcome: Vessel boarded and escorted to Finnish waters. Crew placed under travel bans; criminal proceedings opened.
incidents.why_it_matters: Estlink 2 capacity dropped from 1,016 MW to 358 MW, so the fault is independently visible in grid data as well as in telecom outage feeds. A worked example of corroborating a behavioural detection against a non-AIS source.

incidents.title: Trans-Pacific cable damaged north of Yehliu, northern Taiwan
assets: Chunghwa Telecom international cable (4 cores damaged)
incidents.mechanism: Suspected anchor drag; vessel reported operating two AIS transponder identities and switching between them
incidents.outcome: Coast guard unable to board due to weather. Vessel proceeded to Busan. Shipowner denied involvement. Coast guard said intentions were impossible to confirm but could not rule out grey-zone activity.
incidents.why_it_matters: The reference case for the identity-integrity checks in the dossier. A hull with dual registration, an IMO number not in IMO records, and two transponders will present in a naive single-MMSI view as a clean, innocent gap.

sources.label: Reuters via Yahoo - shipowner denies accusation
Jamestown Foundation - Strangers on a Seabed

incidents.title: Ventspils-Gotland fibre cable damaged
incidents.outcome: Vessel seized, then released. Swedish prosecutors ruled out sabotage.
incidents.why_it_matters: The most important case in this library. Same sea, same season, same mechanism, same initial press framing as the confirmed cases - and it was an accident. Any detection matching this profile should be read against this outcome first.

sources.label: AP via Yahoo - Sweden investigating damaged cable

incidents.title: Taiwan-Penghu cable severed
assets: Taiwan main island to Penghu Islands cable
incidents.mechanism: Loitering in the vicinity of the cable prior to the fault
incidents.outcome: Vessel and Chinese crew detained by the Taiwan Coast Guard, which had been monitoring it for loitering behaviour.
incidents.why_it_matters: Loitering alone triggered the surveillance that produced the interception. Demonstrates the operational value of a low-confidence loiter alert when a watch officer can act on it.

incidents.title: Multiple cables severed in the Red Sea
assets: Reported as up to 15 cable systems affected
incidents.mechanism: Not established; reporting indicates the damage appeared accidental
incidents.outcome: Latency increases and widespread disruption across the Middle East and South Asia.
incidents.why_it_matters: Largest single disruption in the series and the one with the least AIS evidence. A chokepoint outside dense terrestrial receiver coverage is exactly where this tool has least to say.

sources.label: Marine Technology News - Subsea Cable Sabotage

incidents.title: Elisa and Arelion cables, Helsinki to Tallinn
incidents.mechanism: Anchor drag; vessel intercepted with anchor still in the water, seabed tracks running several tens of kilometres
incidents.outcome: Seized by Finnish authorities in the Estonian EEZ while transiting St Petersburg to Haifa. Fourteen crew from Russia, Georgia, Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan detained; two arrested, two travel-banned. Investigated as aggravated criminal damage and aggravated interference with telecommunications.
incidents.why_it_matters: Cleanest labelled positive in the series: intercepted mid-act, with physical seabed evidence and a documented drag length. Use it as the reference track when tuning thresholds.

sources.label: Moscow Times - Finland seizes cargo ship

incidents.title: Sventoji to Liepaja telecom cable damaged
incidents.outcome: Latvian police boarded a ship docked at Liepaja and opened criminal proceedings, then reported finding no evidence linking it to the damage.
incidents.why_it_matters: Second calibration case for false positives: proximity plus timing was enough to justify boarding and not enough to sustain a link.
